description: BoilerAlert as an earth system trend detctive
summary: Buildings waste energy when their systems drift, and this wasted energy adds to the emissions that warm the climate. BoilerAlert closes this loop with NASA data. First, the tool lets the user select NASA variables (air and surface temperature, heat and cold peaks, heating and cooling degree days, satellite surface temperature), plots them from 1996 to 2024 for three cities, and tests if each trend is statistically significant. Then we treat the climate as the signal: we use the NASA daily temperature to predict the ideal electricity consumption of a real building, day by day. When the meter stays above this ideal value for several days, the tool raises an alert so the maintenance team can schedule a check. Less drift means less wasted energy and fewer emissions.
details:
GOAL

Wasted energy in buildings adds to the emissions that warm the climate. We show this warming with NASA data, then use the same climate signal to detect energy drifts in buildings with software only, without adding hardware.

HOW IT WORKS

BoilerAlert is one web page with two parts.

1. Climate trends. The user picks one of seven NASA variables (air and surface temperature, hottest and coldest day of the year, heating and cooling degree days, and satellite surface temperature from AIRS). The tool plots the yearly values for three cities over 29 years (1996 to 2024), computes the trend per decade with a 95% confidence interval, and runs the Mann-Kendall test.

2. Building simulator. We use a real university building in London with two years of electricity readings. A simple model, fitted on the first year, uses the NASA daily temperature to predict what the building should consume. An alert appears when the meter stays more than 15% above this value for 3 days in a row.

RESULTS

- Air temperature rises in the three cities: Besançon +0.67 °C per decade, Marseille +0.58, London +0.35, all significant.

- Heating need falls everywhere, and cooling need rises strongly in Marseille.

- Not every trend is significant: the satellite series for London (22 years) is too short to conclude.

- With the real readings, no false alert over the whole year.

- With a simulated drift of +25%, the alert appears on the third day, with 19,335 kWh of excess over 28 days.

IMPACT

Energy drifts are usually found too late, on the bill or after a breakdown. With the weather as a reference, maintenance teams can act sooner, which cuts wasted energy and emissions.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The detection is done with software, not with new sensors. Sensors must be manufactured, installed and powered, which has a cost and a carbon footprint. BoilerAlert uses only what already exists: the building's meter and free NASA data. A solution meant to reduce emissions should not create new ones.

TOOLS

One HTML file with JavaScript, online at https://simulator-boiler-alert.vercel.app, with nothing to install. The statistics run in the browser and were checked against SciPy. Data: NASA POWER, NASA Giovanni and Building Data Genome Project 2.

LIMITS

One NASA POWER point covers about 50 km, not the exact street. A gap can also come from a change in how the building is used. The drift in the demo is simulated and labelled as simulated.
